newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JULY 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - JULY 1.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
--The dissatisfying course of inflation is now becoming apparent with estimates that inflation currently at 5.4 percent will stall there or even rise slightly in June.
--Government economic experts predict a growth rate of 3.5 percent this year, and 3.7 and 4.1 percent respectively for the next two years.

--The president of Intracom, Greece's most successful telecoms company, yesterday attacked Development Minister Vasso Papandreou for her support last week for a one-off charge that would skim 10 percent off company profits for unemployment. Business needs tax breaks to create new jobs, not new taxes, Socrates Kokkalis said.

--Government, unions and employers will look at the status of the eight-hour working day today during 'social dialogue' on changes to the job market. The government aims at greater flexibility in the spread of working hours and hopes to be able to deregulate the eight-hour working day to satisfy demand without having to pay overtime.

--National prototypyes are no longer able to meet the new challenges thrown up by the dramatic changes in the social and economic sectors in European unification, Prime Minister Costas Simitis said yesterday, speaking after talks with Jacques Delors, the former European Commission president.

--Satellite communications will soon be deregulated, Macedonia-Thrace Minister Philippos Petsalnikos said yesterday at a function on the development of communication as a condition for economic growth at the Italian Chamber of Commerce in Thessaloniki.
--ETEBA investment bank will distribute one new share for each ten to shareholders, following a decision at the bank's general assembly yesterday.

--Realism and vision is the challenge facing European socialists, according to Simitis and Delors, who both spoke yesterday on "The Europe we want". "We have to be realists in our policies but visionaries in our goals," Simitis said.
--Following a buyout of the Appollonio Clinic, the Apostolopoulos Group is now looking to enter the insurance area by the purchase of an insurance firm involved in life and accident coverage.

--Drastic cutbacks in public expenditures and the lack of margins for new taxes mean drastic measures as of September, according to National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. The first decisions on the mergers or abolitions of public organisations and enterprises will come after the expert committee on the issue drafts its report. Changes are also expected in public transportation. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
